newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn's Stark says govt not to sell off loans.
newsitem.headline: Bonn's Stark says govt not to sell off loans.

text.p: Juergen Stark, state secretary in the German finance ministry, said on Tuesday the German government had no intention of selling loans made to foreign countries to German banks to help ease Bonn's debt position.
"You can imagine that there are considerations taking place in many areas to help the government in its difficult situation," Stark said.
"But we have no intention of selling third-country liabilities, whatever the terms may be," he said.

Stark's comments came in response to weekend news reports that said the Bonn government was contemplating whether to sell off debt to the banks to help whip its finances into shape to meet entry criteria for European monetary union.
Stark was speaking at a news conference at the Bundesbank called to announce the issuance of a new strippable 30-year bond.
